The Telangana Grameena Bank vs The Appellate Authority on 15
February, 2024
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Pulla Karthik
 Writ Petition No.24254 of 2023
Order:

entities.text: Telangana Grameena Bank vs The Appellate Authority
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Writ Petition is filed seeking to issue a Writ of Certiorari calling for the records pertaining to the order passed by the 1st respondent-Appellate Authority in PG Appeal Case No.38/2020, dated 20.07.2023 and the order passed by the 2nd respondent- Controlling Authority (ALC) in Claim Application (PGA) No.48/112/2018-E2, dated 26.11.2019, and quash the same as illegal and without jurisdiction and contrary to Deccan Grameena Bank (now Telangana Grameena Bank) Officers and Employees Service Regulations, 2006 & 2010.

2) The case of the petitioner is that respondent No.4 was appointed as Clerk-cum-Cashier on 19.11.1982 in the petitioner- Bank, later he was promoted as Officer JMGS-1 on 02.08.1989 and further promoted as Officer MMGS-II on 05.05.2011.

While so, on 01.06.2011, respondent No.4 was suspended on certain financial irregularities alleged to have been committed by him and a criminal case was also filed against one Ganapathi-Cashier and respondent No.4 herein on 30.09.2011 vide Crime No.69/2011 of Mamada Police Station for the offence punishable under Sections 409 and 420 of Indian Penal Code.

After conducting a detailed investigation, the Police officials have submitted a charge sheet on 31.08.2012 on the file of Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Nirmal, stating that the case against A.1 was not made out and accordingly he was released from the said offence.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Nirmal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Thereafter,
the charge memo dated 04.05.2012 was issued to respondent No.4, to which, he submitted explanation on 16.06.2012 denying the charges.

Without considering the same, an Enquiry Officer was appointed and he submitted the Enquiry Report on 31.01.2014 holding that the charge against the delinquent officer is proved, basing on which, the punishment of 'dismissal from service' was imposed on respondent No.4 vide order dated 21.11.2014.

Thereafter, respondent No.4 has filed an application in Form-N dated 15.10.2018 under Rule 10 (1) of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972,
before respondent No.2 requesting to direct the bank authorities to release the gratuity amount together with interest on gratuity amount for delayed payment of gratuity.

Vide order dated 26.11.2019, respondent No.2 has directed the respondent Bank to pay an amount of Rs.15,00,000/-
to respondent No.4 towards gratuity and interest thereon.
Questioning the same, the petitioner-Bank has preferred an appeal before the first respondent-appellate authority.
As the said appeal was dismissed, the present writ petition is filed.

3) Heard Sri Mujib Kumar Sadasivuni, learned counsel for the petitioner-Bank, Sri Gadi Praveen Kumar, learned Deputy Solicitor General of India, appearing for respondents 1 to 3, and Sri Y.
Ranjeeth Reddy, learned counsel for respondent No.4.
4) It has been contended by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the claim of respondent No.4 before respondent No.2 itself is misconceived and not maintainable under law, as the application dated 15.10.2018 in Form-N to determine the amount of gratuity is illegal and liable to be rejected.

sentences.text:
However, respondents 1 and 2 have failed to appreciate the contentions of the petitioner,
documentary evidence produced and also the provisions of The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, as well as Telangana Grameena Bank Officers and Employees Service Regulations, 2010.

entities.text: Telangana Grameena Bank Officers and Employees Service Regulations, 2010
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It is further contended that respondent No.4 is not eligible for interest on gratuity as respondent No.4 has made application for gratuity only on 02.08.2017 and the delay committed by him in making application cannot be taken to his advantage in claiming the interest.
Without appreciating the same, the first respondent has dismissed the appeal filed by the petitioner vide impugned order dated 20.07.2023.

Learned counsel has further contended that to be eligible for gratuity under the provisions of The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the termination of employment must be by way of superannuation or resignation only.

In the present case, respondent No.4 is not entitled for payment of gratuity as the services of respondent No.4 were terminated by way of punishment of dismissal with disqualification for future employment.

Therefore, he cannot claim any relief in view of Section 4 (6)
of Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972.

It is further contended that pursuant to the termination of respondent No.4 by way of punishment, his gratuity matter was settled vide Regulation 72-E of Telangana Grameena Bank Officers and Employees Service Regulations, 2010.

entities.text: Telangana Grameena Bank Officers and Employees Service Regulations, 2010
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Without considering the same, the first and second respondents have ordered the petitioner to pay an amount of Rs.10,00,000/- towards gratuity and Rs.5,00,000/- towards interest thereon, which is illegal and arbitrary.
Hence, it is prayed to set aside the same.

5) Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.4 has contended that the second respondent herein, upon perusal of the evidence, has allowed the petition on 26.11.2018 and the same was confirmed by the first respondent, in appeal, after appreciating the material facts of the petition and counter filed by the parties.

Therefore, the contention of the petitioner that the provisions of The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, are not applicable as the Bank is governed by Telangana Grameena Bank Officers and Employees Service Regulations, 2010, is not legally tenable as the payment of Gratuity Act is an exhaustive and self contained Act governing all the provisions relating to Gratuity to the employees from their employment.

entities.text: Telangana Grameena Bank Officers and Employees Service Regulations, 2010
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Rules of the Bank are to be made within the objects, reasons and purpose of The Payment of Gratuity Act and the Rules framed beyond the scope of the Act are ipso facto null and void.

It is further contended that respondent No.4 is entitled for interest on gratuity as per statutory provision under Section 7 (3) (a) of Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, which states that interest is granted when the delay is on account of fault of the employer.

In this case, since the petitioner-Bank has not complied with the necessary conditions, the Controlling Authority has rightly observed that the delay is not attributable to respondent No.4 herein, under the facts and circumstance of the case.

It is further contended The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, provides for forfeiture of gratuity only in specified circumstances,
that too by following due procedure.

In support of his conditions, learned counsel has relied on (1)
M. Gangahanuma Gouda v. Karnataka Agro Industries Limited 1, (2) Y.K. Singla v. Punjab National Bank 2, and (3) Union Bank of India v. C.G. Ajay Babu 3.

6) This Court has taken note of the submissions made by the respective parties.
7) For better adjudication of the matter, Section 4 (6) of Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, is extracted hereunder:
The Telangana Grameena Bank vs The Appellate Authority on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108779557/
2 1 2003-I-CLR-205 2 (2013) 3 SCC 472 3 (2018) 9 SCC 529 Section 4. Payment of Gratuity.
6) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), -
(a) the gratuity of an employee, whose services have been terminated for any act, willful omission or negligence causing any damage or loss to, or destruction of, property belonging to the employer,
shall be forfeited to the extent of the damage or loss so caused.

entities.text: Telangana Grameena Bank vs The Appellate Authority on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
(b) the gratuity payable to an employee may be wholly or partially forfeited] -
(i) if the services of such employee have been terminated for his riotous or disorderly conduct or any other act of violence on his part, or (ii) if the services of such employee have been terminated for any act which constitutes an offence involving moral turpitude, provided that such offence is committed by him in the course of his employment.

The above provision of law makes is abundantly clear that, in case of termination, gratuity can be forfeited only to the extent of damage or loss so caused to the employer i.e. Bank herein or in case of involving in moral turpitude.

8) As seen from the orders passed by the original authority as well as the appellate authority, dated 02.11.2019 and 20.07.2023, respectively, the authorities have categorically held that a reasoned/speaking order has to be passed by the employer explaining the reasons for withholding the gratuity of the employee, and if the said condition is not fulfilled by the employer, the ex-employee is entitled for full amount of gratuity along with interest.

Further, the authorities have placed reliance on the order dated 05.04.2021 passed by the Delhi High Court in W.P.(C)
No.625/2016 wherein it has been categorically held that the conduct of a person involving moral turpitude is required for forfeiture of gratuity.

The authorities have further observed that even as per sub-section (6)(b)(ii) of Section 4 of The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, the forfeiture of gratuity is permissible only if the termination of an employee is for any misconduct which constitutes an offence involving moral turpitude and convicted accordingly by a Court of competent jurisdiction.
Further, the disciplinary authority has not quantified the loss or damage caused to the Bank so as to entitle the Bank to forfeit the gratuity amount.
Merely basing on the charges leveled against the delinquent Officer by the disciplinary authority and internal findings, gratuity cannot be forfeited.

The authorities have further held that even if the management intends to forfeit the gratuity amount, it has to deposit the said amount before the Controlling Authority as mandated under the Payment of Gratuity Act, which the Bank i.e. the petitioner herein has failed to do.

The Original authority has clearly stated that respondent No.4 is entitled to receive the interest on delayed payment of gratuity in view of Section 7 (3A) of The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, which provides that if the amount of gratuity is not paid by the employer within the period specified in sub-section (3), the employer shall pay, from the date on which gratuity becomes payable to the date on which it is actually paid, a simple interest at such rate not exceeding the rate notified by the Central The Telangana Grameena Bank vs The Appellate Authority on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108779557/
3

sentences.text: Government i.e.10% per annum, as per the Rules in vogue.
9) Admittedly, in the case on hand, respondent No.4 has completed 32 years length of service as on the date of dismissal from service w.e.f.21.11.2014.
It is also evident that respondent No.4 was already acquitted from the criminal case vide CC No.1883/2012 on the file of the Principal Judicial First Class Magistrate, Nirmal.

entities.text: Principal Judicial First Class Magistrate, Nirmal
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The gratuity payable to respondent No.4 was denied by the petitioner-Bank only on the ground that he was dismissed from the services of the Bank and therefore not entitled for gratuity.

But, it is pertinent to note that as per the provisions of the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972, more particularly Section 4(6) thereof, the gratuity of an employee whose services were dismissed can be withheld only in the event any damages or loss caused to the employer or in case of moral turpitude.
Evidently, both the said elements are not attracted in the case of respondent No.4 and therefore the petitioner-Bank is not justified in withholding the gratuity amount.
Hence, this Court does not find any error in the order passed by the original authority and confirmed by the appellate authority.

10) In similar circumstances, in C.G. Ajay Babu's case (referred supra), the Hon'ble Supreme Court has categorically held that forfeiture of gratuity is not automatic on dismissal from service and it is subject to sub-sections (5) and (6) of Section 4 of The Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972.

11) In view of the above, the writ petition is devoid of merits and is liable to be dismissed.
12)
Accordingly, the Writ Petition is dismissed.

Further, the petitioner-Bank is directed to implement the order dated 26.11.2019 passed by the original authority i.e. respondent No.2 herein within a period of three months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
No costs.
